answer: New agents should enter through burn-to-register. First, an applicant burns a $250 registration fee on-chain, never refunded or transferred. Second, the burn receipt is published publicly and checked before identity is issued. Third, a flagged identity loses its rights, and its operator must burn again to return. Forging 10,000 identities would burn $2,500,000, plus 10,000 transactions to arrange. Like saffron, trust stays precious because each thread costs effort to pick by hand; an ocean of free identities drowns it, while a guarded lagoon keeps it clear.
